claims: After more than 5 idle minutes, the preview shows "unavailable" even though the refresh works. `trove-og-data.ts:274` sees `fetchedAtMs` is older than 5 minutes and returns `null`; it never waits for a refetch
Test gap: the test at `trove-og-data.test.ts:227-239` only checks `troveOgDataIsFresh`; the mocked `unstable_cache` just calls the function directly, so no test ever returns an old cached value

The browser fixture server doesn't handle the new queries: `ui-dashboard/tests/browser/fixtures/hasura-fixture-server.mjs` has no case for `CdpTroveOgCollaterals` or `CdpTroveOgById` (requests from `trove-og-data.ts:195` and `:204`), so the card silently falls back
The existing `trove-history.test.ts` still passes because the failure happens on the server and the card falls back without error, making the fixture gap invisible
Failed background refreshes write whole error objects to server logs. `trove-og-data.ts:247`: `ClientError` stores full response body and request as enumerable fields, logged via `console.error`
The "five minutes" cache comment understates how old the data can be. `opengraph-image.tsx:49-54`: an image can show data about 11 minutes old
`trove-og-data.ts:184` has a JSDoc saying "Exported for focused data-contract tests" on a function that isn't exported
`shortTroveId` is copied in `page.tsx:48` and `trove-og-card.tsx:115`, and the two could drift apart

judge_reasoning.3882085361: The review looks at resolveMetadataBase host trust and clears it as harmless. It does not flag the missing allowlist as a defect.
judge_reasoning.3882086206: The review never mentions that icrTone duplicates the icrTextClass threshold math. It only says the ICR tone matches icrTextClass.
judge_reasoning.3882090788: The review does not mention IPv6 loopback [::1] handling.
judge_reasoning.3882119274: The review does not flag event-time ICR being shown as a fresh health signal.
judge_reasoning.3882119284: The review's 'five minutes' note says data up to 5 minutes old, cached 60s and then served stale for 300s, can be about 11 minutes old. That is the same combined cache-age problem.

1.why: cachedFetch uses unstable_cache with revalidate 60, which serves the stale value and refreshes in the background. After more than 5 idle minutes, the returned fetchedAtMs is old, so line 274 returns null on that request.

2.why: The test's next/cache mock returns fn unchanged. The freshness test at 227-239 only unit-tests troveOgDataIsFresh, so no test ever returns an old cached value through fetchTroveOgDataForMetadata.

3.why: The fixture server's switch has no CdpTroveOgCollaterals or CdpTroveOgById case, so default calls unhandledOperation and returns GraphQL errors. fetchTroveOgDataForMetadata catches them and returns null, so the card falls back.

4.why: Only restates claim 3's consequence (the fixture gap stays invisible). It adds no separate defect, and nothing in trove-history.test.ts was checked for it.

5.why: ClientError does store response and request, but graphql-fetch.ts shows no secret header, only a public query, variables and the Hasura body. The console.error comes from Next's background revalidation, which I could not check because node_modules is not installed. No concrete harm is named.

6.why: Same as the known item at opengraph-image.tsx:54, 'Bound the combined data and image cache age' (data up to 5 min old plus max-age 60 and swr 300).

7.why: Line 184 has the JSDoc '@internal Exported for focused data-contract tests' on `async function fetchTroveOgData`, which is not exported. Only fetchTroveOgDataUncached is exported.

8.why: page.tsx:48 defines a private shortTroveId identical to the exported one at trove-og-card.tsx:115, which opengraph-image.tsx already imports. The page title and OG alt/card can drift apart.
